value.stringValue: The unrestricted org default. Every FQS install ships with this as the org-wide default so the platform's activate-schedule action has a fallback designation.
Internal designation, not a donor restriction. The board has earmarked these funds internally but can undesignate at will. The donor imposed no restriction.
A reserve is money held back for future need, spendable if the board votes to release. Distinct from Board Designated Fund. Teaches that Without Donor Restriction does not mean unspoken for.

Catch-all for gifts a donor restricted to programs broadly without naming a specific program. When a donor restricts a gift toward this designation to a specific timeframe (e.g., FY2027), record the boundary on the gift's Restriction Release Date, not on this designation.

Generic placeholder for a purpose-restricted program designation. Rename to one of your actual programs after install. When a donor restricts a gift toward this designation to a specific timeframe (e.g., FY2027), record the boundary on the gift's Restriction Release Date, not on this designation.

Generic placeholder for a second purpose-restricted program designation. Rename to one of your actual programs after install. When a donor restricts a gift toward this designation to a specific timeframe (e.g., FY2027), record the boundary on the gift's Restriction Release Date, not on this designation.

Distinct purpose from ongoing programs: growth or new-initiative capacity. Donors give here specifically to launch something new. When a donor restricts a gift toward this designation to a specific timeframe (e.g., FY2027), record the boundary on the gift's Restriction Release Date, not on this designation.

Purpose can be tangible non-capital spending: below-capitalization-threshold equipment, consumable supplies. Distinct from Capital Campaign Fund (above the capitalization threshold). When a donor restricts a gift toward this designation to a specific timeframe (e.g., FY2027), record the boundary on the gift's Restriction Release Date, not on this designation.

Purpose can be donor-restricted personnel costs. Teaches that programs and salaries are separable purposes: a donor may fund a specific role without funding the surrounding program. When a donor restricts a gift toward this designation to a specific timeframe (e.g., FY2027), record the boundary on the gift's Restriction Release Date, not on this designation.

Capital-project purpose (building, renovation, major equipment above the capitalization threshold). Capital gifts release when the asset is placed in service, not on a schedule. When a donor restricts a gift toward this designation to a specific timeframe (e.g., FY2027), record the boundary on the gift's Restriction Release Date, not on this designation.
Endowment principal is held indefinitely; only earnings are spendable. Add named endowments (e.g., Smith Family Scholarship Endowment) as your program grows.
Exchange-transaction revenue: gala ticket sales, event registration, workshop admission. Distinct from a donation given AT an event, this is what the ticket itself was worth.
Sale of goods: t-shirts, books, branded items. Exchange transaction, not a contribution. The buyer received something of equivalent value.
Program-related fee revenue: participation fees, consulting retainers, service delivery charges. Distinct from a program-restricted donation (which lives in General Program or a named Program).

Flow.description: Setup-time Screen Flow that seeds a starter Gift Designation catalog. Admin picks which starter designations to create; flow inserts them via recordCreates. Runs from FQS Setup Flow chooser or as a standalone Setup step. Ships 14 curated starter entries across the four restriction categories. v3 adds idempotency: queries existing designations by Name and silently skips any already present in the org, so the flow can be re-run without creating duplicates. Org-default swap remains in a follow-up.
Flow.label: FQS Suggest Designations

fields.name: DisplayText_Intro
fields.fieldText:
Welcome. This tool seeds a starter Gift Designation catalog for your org.


Fundraising Quick Start ships a curated set of Gift Designation records so gift entry can filter by donor restriction and default to an org-wide fallback.


On the next screen, pick which starter designations you want. You can rename or retire any of them later from the Designation record page.


This release ships 14 starter entries across the four restriction categories: Without Donor Restriction, With Donor Restriction - Purpose, With Donor Restriction - Permanent, and Earned Revenue.

fields.name: DisplayText_Pick_Intro
fields.fieldText:
Tick the starter designations you want in your org. Each is grouped by restriction category. All are pre-selected; uncheck any you do not want.


A note on time restrictions: FQS deliberately does not offer a "With Donor Restriction - Time" category on the designation. A designation names what the money is for, not when it becomes spendable. Time boundaries (e.g., FY2027, or "hold until the building opens") belong on the individual gift instead, on the Restriction Release Date field on the Gift Commitment or Gift Transaction. That lets one purpose-restricted designation (e.g., "Building Fund") carry gifts with many different release dates without proliferating year-suffixed designations.

fields.fieldText:
No designations were selected.


Nothing was created. Click Previous to pick at least one, or Finish to exit without creating any designations.

fields.name: DisplayText_Success
fields.fieldText:
Your Gift Designation catalog is seeded.


You can retire any of these at any time by setting IsActive = FALSE on the record page. Retired designations remain queryable and remain valid for back-dated gifts.


This flow is safe to re-run. Any starter designation already in your org (matched by exact Name) is skipped, and only the new picks are created. Re-run any time to add designations you unchecked earlier.

fields.name: DisplayText_Fault
fields.fieldText:
The flow could not create the selected designations.


Common causes:

  • Your permission set does not grant Create on Gift Designation. Ensure FQS Custom Fields (or an equivalent permset) is assigned.
  • An org-wide default is already set on another Gift Designation. Only one Gift Designation can carry IsDefault = TRUE at a time.
  • A validation rule or trigger on Gift Designation rejected the insert.


Close this flow, resolve the cause, and relaunch it.


Fault message: {!$Flow.FaultMessage}
